rows.experiment_summary: The experiment tested an RNA-only model using PCA encoding on single-profile data, isolating RNA modality as the sole input. Validation accuracy of 0.485 and F1 of 0.464 suggest RNA-only models achieve moderate baseline performance. Uncertainty remains about how this baseline compares to multimodal configurations or more complex encodings, as no alternative designs have been evaluated yet.
rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should establish a baseline. Validation accuracy of 0.520 and F1 of 0.498 suggest a slight improvement over the previous PCA encoder baseline. Uncertainty remains about how this performance compares to multimodal configurations or other encoding strategies, as no such comparisons have been evaluated.

rows.experiment_summary: This experiment tested an RNA-only model using scvi_n200 encoder with multiprofile data and avgpool aggregation, comparing against the singleprofile baseline. Validation accuracy of 0.650 (F1: 0.628) suggests improved performance over previous RNA-only models, indicating potential benefits from multiprofile data or aggregation method. Uncertainty remains about the relative contribution of profile setting vs. aggregation, and how this compares to multimodal configurations or alternative encodings.
rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence shows scvi_n200 (config_004) outperforms PCA (config_001) in RNA-only singleprofile models. This experiment tests whether using multiprofile data with scvi_n200 (config_005) improves performance, isolating the impact of profile setting and aggregation method (avgpool). It directly compares to the current RNA-only baseline while exploring a key design decision (multiprofile vs singleprofile) with minimal additional complexity.

rows.experiment_summary: This experiment tested a multimodal model combining RNA (pca_n2000) and image (resnet50) data with concat fusion, comparing against RNA-only multiprofile baselines. Validation accuracy (0.6186) and F1 (0.6103) are lower than the RNA-only multiprofile model (0.6501), suggesting multimodal fusion may not improve performance in this setup. Uncertainty remains about the effectiveness of concat fusion and the relative contribution of image data, as no alternative fusion strategies or encoder combinations have been evaluated.
rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence shows RNA-only multiprofile models (config_005) achieve 0.65 accuracy, suggesting multiprofile data and aggregation improve performance. This experiment tests adding image data (resnet50) to the same RNA encoder (pca_n2000) and aggregation (avgpool) setup, isolating the effect of multimodal fusion. It directly compares multimodal vs. RNA-only in a consistent baseline, addressing uncertainty about whether combining modalities improves performance.

rows.experiment_summary: This experiment tested a multimodal model using weighted fusion (vs. concat in config_018) with RNA (pca_n2000) and image (resnet50) data, achieving validation accuracy of 0.639 (F1: 0.620). The result suggests weighted fusion may offer marginal improvement over concat, though performance remains lower than the RNA-only multiprofile baseline (0.650). Uncertainty persists about the relative effectiveness of fusion strategies and the contribution of image data, as no other fusion methods or encoder combinations have been evaluated.
rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence shows RNA-only multiprofile models (config_005) achieve 0.650 accuracy, while multimodal config_018 (0.618) underperforms. This experiment tests weighted fusion (vs. concat in config_018) to isolate whether fusion strategy impacts performance. It addresses uncertainty about multimodal effectiveness and isolates fusion method as a variable, balancing exploration of critical design choices without overcomplicating the model.

rows.experiment_summary: This experiment tested RNA-only multiprofile models using transformer aggregation instead of avgpool, with pca_n2000 encoder. Validation accuracy of 0.519 is lower than the avgpool baseline (0.650), suggesting transformer aggregation may not improve performance. Uncertainty remains about the relative effectiveness of aggregation methods and whether other factors like image modality could enhance results, as no alternative fusion strategies have been evaluated.
rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence shows RNA-only multiprofile models with avgpool aggregation (config_005) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.650). This experiment tests transformer aggregation in the same RNA-only multiprofile setup with pca_n2000 encoder, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It directly compares transformer vs avgpool, helping determine if aggregation strategy significantly impacts performance. This is critical for understanding whether improving aggregation could surpass the current RNA-only baseline or if other factors (like image modality) are needed.

rows.experiment_summary: This experiment tested an RNA-only model using scgpt encoder in a multiprofile setup with avgpool aggregation, comparing against the scvi_n200 baseline (config_005). Validation accuracy (0.530) and F1 (0.515) are lower than the scvi_n200 baseline (0.650), suggesting scgpt may not improve performance in this configuration. Uncertainty remains about whether other factors, such as encoder-specific characteristics or hyperparameters, contributed to the difference, and how this compares to alternative encoders or aggregation strategies.
rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence shows RNA-only multiprofile models with avgpool aggregation (config_005: 0.650 accuracy) outperform singleprofile and other encoders. This experiment tests scgpt encoder in the same multiprofile/avgpool setup, isolating the RNA encoder's impact. It clarifies whether scgpt (a more advanced encoder) improves performance compared to scvi_n200, directly addressing a key design choice with minimal changes to the proven baseline.

rows.experiment_summary: This experiment tested RNA-only multiprofile models using scvi_n200 encoder with transformer aggregation, comparing against the avgpool aggregation baseline (config_003). Validation accuracy of 0.653 (F1: 0.628) shows a marginal improvement over the avgpool baseline (0.650), suggesting transformer aggregation may offer slight benefits. Uncertainty remains about the statistical significance of this improvement and whether other factors, such as encoder-specific characteristics, could influence the result, as no alternative fusion strategies or encoder combinations have been evaluated.
rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence shows RNA-only multiprofile models with scvi_n200 encoder (config_005) achieve the highest accuracy (0.650). This experiment tests the same RNA encoder with transformer aggregation to isolate the effect of aggregation method. It clarifies whether transformer aggregation (used in config_003 with lower performance) is suboptimal or if the RNA encoder's quality dominates. This addresses a key design choice (aggregation) without changing other variables, balancing exploration of critical components while building on the strongest RNA-only baseline.

rows.experiment_summary: This experiment tested a multimodal model using the advanced imagenet_vit_l image encoder instead of resnet50, maintaining pca_n2000 RNA encoding, avgpool aggregation, and concat fusion. Validation accuracy of 0.629 (F1: 0.599) is slightly higher than the resnet50-based multimodal baseline (config_004: 0.6186) but remains lower than the RNA-only multiprofile baseline (config_003: 0.650). Uncertainty persists about whether the improved image encoder sufficiently compensates for the multimodal setup's inherent challenges and how fusion/encoding choices interact.
rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence shows RNA-only multiprofile models (config_005: 0.650 accuracy) outperform multimodal resnet50-based models (config_019: 0.639). This experiment tests whether using a more advanced image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) in a multimodal setup with multiprofile data and avgpool aggregation can improve performance. It isolates the effect of the image encoder, a key design choice, to determine if better image representations could bridge the gap between RNA-only and multimodal performance.

rows.experiment_summary: This experiment tested an RNA-only multiprofile model using pca_n2000 encoder, comparing against the scvi_n200 baseline (config_003). Validation accuracy of 0.591 (F1: 0.573) is lower than the scvi_n200 model's 0.650, suggesting the scvi_n200 encoder's performance advantage persists in multiprofile data. Uncertainty remains about whether pca_n2000 could achieve similar performance with alternative configurations or if other RNA encoders might yield better results.
rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence shows RNA-only multiprofile models with scvi_n200 encoder (config_005) achieve the highest accuracy (0.650). It clarifies whether the scvi_n200 encoder's performance advantage (vs pca_n2000 in singleprofile) persists in multiprofile data, directly addressing uncertainty about encoder importance while maintaining consistency in aggregation and profile settings.
